findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - build or run CI for either newly created starter.
`forge init` supplies the `.dockerignore` from `src/forge/templates/skeleton/.dockerignore:4`, which excludes `**/.npmrc`, including the root file. This new COPY and `src/forge/templates/starter-python/Dockerfile:6` nevertheless require that file. Docker therefore fails before installing dependencies, blocking both starter image builds and the client checks that build them. The ignore rule also protects apps that put credentials in `.npmrc`, so making the file available to the build would need to preserve that protection.
findings.title: Starter image builds try to copy an ignored .npmrc

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - run a starter's client check twice on GitHub-hosted runners with unchanged lockfiles.
The owner-approved item is: “On a second run with an unchanged lockfile, the client check reuses downloaded packages and image layers, and a source-only edit no longer reinstalls the packages in the image build.” The ruling says the generated workflow does not build images, but the client test commands do: `src/forge/templates/starter/scripts/test.mjs:56` and `src/forge/templates/starter-python/scripts/test.mjs:53` run Docker Compose with `--build`. That evidence was not accounted for by the ruling. Hosted jobs start with fresh builders, and the workflow exports or restores no Docker build cache, so the image layers are rebuilt on the second run. Also, `setup-uv@v6` [prunes downloaded wheels by default](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/v6/README.md#disable-cache-pruning); the Python starter locks such wheels, for example at `src/forge/templates/starter-python/apps/api/uv.lock:19`, so they are downloaded again.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - create a feature in a new TypeScript starter and build its image.
The install layer copies only the starter's fixed manifest list. `src/forge/feature.py:140` creates additional contracts and server packages, and `src/forge/feature.py:170` adds the new server as an API workspace dependency, but neither new manifest is present when pnpm installs. Their workspace dependencies are consequently not installed for the image build. The Python Dockerfile has the same fixed-list limitation for added workspace packages at `src/forge/templates/starter-python/Dockerfile:12`. Conversely, removing an unused starter module also makes its unconditional COPY fail.
findings.title: Install all workspace manifests when an app adds a feature

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - sync an existing pnpm app that installs its own pinned pnpm version in its test command and has no root `packageManager` field.
Every detected `pnpm-lock.yaml` now adds this action without a version input. The [action's v4 contract](https://github.com/pnpm/action-setup/blob/v4/README.md#version) requires either that input or a `packageManager` field, so it fails before the app's test command can install pnpm. Both pull-request tests and the full suite become red after sync, although the existing app's package-manager setup has not changed. The adopted-client test exercises only npm.
findings.title: Do not require a pnpm packageManager field in adopted clients

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Moving part
Case: normal use - run any generated pnpm client check.
The workflow now depends on the separate third-party `pnpm/action-setup` GitHub Action, but the fix's New moving parts line says none. The starters already pin pnpm and invoke it through Corepack (`src/forge/templates/starter/package.json:84` and `src/forge/templates/starter/scripts/test.mjs:46`); the Done-when item does not name this additional action. Remove the extra dependency or obtain an owner-approved moving-part decision.
findings.title: Moving part: pnpm/action-setup

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a future Dockerfile change copies application source before the install layer.
The named proof only searches generated workflow and Dockerfile text; it never observes a second cache hit or rebuild. For example, inserting `COPY apps ./apps` before the install leaves these assertions passing while every application source edit invalidates the dependency layer. The existing live smoke builds once (`tests/test_starter_tree.py:233`); after its source edit it only lists commands (`tests/test_starter_tree.py:319`). Thus neither check proves the promised reuse for either starter.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_new_client_reuses_packages_and_dependency_layers

why: Every client CI run downloads packages again because the generated workflow caches packages only for Forge itself, and both starter web builds copy all source before installing packages, so a source edit reinstalls every package.
